map.莫氏硬度常见宝石参考：琥珀与珍珠 2.5 至 4、珊瑚 3 至 4、青金石 5: Mohs hardness reference for common gems: amber and pearl 2.5–4, coral 3–4, lapis lazuli 5–6, Hetian jade 6–6.5, jadeite 6.5–7, quartz and agate 7, tourmaline 7–7.5, spinel 8, ruby/sapphire and topaz 8–9, diamond 10; gems below 5 are not for daily wear, 5–7 should avoid friction with hard objects, and 8 or above suit daily wear; gems both at Mohs 7 may still scratch each other due to different cleavage directions, so equal hardness does not mean they can be stacked freely.
map.由德国矿物学家莫斯(Friedrich Mohs)于1812年提出，以10种标准: Proposed by German mineralogist Friedrich Mohs in 1812, using 10 standard minerals as references to express a mineral's resistance to scratching.
map.1滑石 → 2石膏 → 3方解石 → 4萤石 → 5磷灰石 → 6正长石 → 7: 1 Talc → 2 Gypsum → 3 Calcite → 4 Fluorite → 5 Apatite → 6 Orthoclase → 7 Quartz → 8 Topaz → 9 Corundum → 10 Diamond.
map.硬度≥7适合日常佩戴(耐刮擦)；硬度6-7需小心使用；硬度<6仅适合耳环、吊坠等: Hardness ≥ 7 suits daily wear (scratch-resistant); 6–7 needs careful use; below 6 only suits earrings, pendants, and other low-impact jewelry, avoiding contact with hard objects.
map.按莫氏硬度判断宝石耐刮与佩戴场景。: Use Mohs hardness to judge gem scratch-resistance and wear scenarios.
map.避免硬物混放互相刮花。: Avoid storing hard objects together to prevent scratching.
map.钻石 10、红蓝宝(刚玉) 9、托帕石 8–8.5、石英 7–7.5、珍珠/珊瑚: Diamond 10, ruby/sapphire (corundum) 9, topaz 8–8.5, quartz 7–7.5, pearl/coral about 3–4 (soft organic gems). A hardness gap of ≥2 grades is needed for obvious mutual scratching.
map.珍珠硬度仅 3–4，与金属或硬石同盒会被划伤；应软布分隔存放，远离 7 级以上宝: Pearls are only 3–4 on the hardness scale and get scratched in the same box as metal or hard stones; store them separated by soft cloth, away from gems above 7.
map.不是等比。10 级是 ordinal 排序，钻石(10)远超刚玉(9)的差距远大: Not proportional. The 10 grades are an ordinal ranking; the gap between diamond (10) and corundum (9) far exceeds that between 9 and 8, and it only indicates whether they can scratch each other.
map.硬度高就不怕摔吗？: Is high hardness safe from breaking?
map.不是。莫氏硬度只代表抗刮擦（划痕）能力，不代表韧性（抗碎裂）。钻石硬度 10 但: No. Mohs hardness only indicates scratch resistance, not toughness (crack resistance). Diamond at 10 has perfect cleavage and can shatter along cleavage planes under heavy impact; jadeite at only 6.5–7 is extremely tough and impact-resistant; fluorite at 4 is very brittle. Daily wear should focus more on toughness — for example emerald at 7.5–8 is brittle with many fissures and must avoid ultrasonic cleaning and impacts.
